query: Let `F : C ⥤ D` be a functor between sites equipped with precoverages `J` on `C` and `K` on `D` that are stable under base change and have pullbacks. If `F` preserves the (pairwise) pullbacks of every `J`-covering and the image of every `J`-covering under `F` is a `K`-covering, then `F` is continuous for the Grothendieck topologies generated by `J` and `K` — i.e. the pullback `F.op ⋙ G` of any sheaf `G` on `(D, K_top)` is a sheaf on `(C, J_top)`.

    13  /-!
    14  # Generators of a Grothendieck topology
    15  
    16  Let `K` be a precoverage and `J` a Grothendieck topology on a category `C`. We
    17  say `K` generates `J` if for every presheaf `F` on `C`, it is a sheaf for `J` if and only
    18  if it is a sheaf for every covering in `K`.
    19  
    20  If `K` generates `J`, then `J` is the smallest Grothendieck topology containing `K`. The converse
    21  only holds if `K` is a coverage or a pretopology.
    22  
    23  ## Implementation details
    24  
    25  For `C : Type u` and `Category.{v} C`, the definition of `Precoverage.Generates` quantifies over
    26  presheafs `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type max u v`. We then show that this implies that the condition holds
    27  for all presheafs `Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w`.
    28  -/
    29  
    30  @[expose] public section
    31  
    32  universe t t' w v u
    33  
    34  namespace CategoryTheory
    35  
    36  variable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] {A : Type*} [Category* A]
    37    {K : Precoverage C} {J : GrothendieckTopology C}

    39  namespace Precoverage
    40  
    41  /-- A precoverage `K` generates the topology `J` if a presheaf on `C` is a sheaf
    42  for `K` if and only if it is a sheaf for `J`. -/

    52    H.le_toPrecoverage _ h

    54  private lemma Generates.isSheaf_of_forall_aux (h : K.Generates J) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)

    71  lemma Generates.isSheaf_of_forall (h : K.Generates J) (F : Cᵒᵖ ⥤ Type w)
    72      (H : ∀ ⦃X : C⦄, ∀ R ∈ K X, Presieve.IsSheafFor F R) :

    20  
    21  We define the notion of continuous functor between sites: these are functors `F` such that
    22  the precomposition with `F.op` preserves sheaves of types (and actually sheaves in any
    23  category).
    24  
    25  ## Main definitions
    26  
    27  * `Functor.IsContinuous`: a functor between sites is continuous if the
    28    precomposition with this functor preserves sheaves with values in

    32    part of a morphism of sites, this would be understood as the pushforward functor
    33    even though it goes in the opposite direction as the functor `G`. (Here, the auxiliary
    34    universe `t` in the assumption that `G` is continuous is the one such that morphisms
    35    in the category `A` are in `Type t`.)
